header:
Date: 2027-09-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Gonzalez (QueryWorks Head of Search), Tom Reilly (QueryWorks Staff SWE), Priya Nair (QueryWorks Product)
summary: Redwood hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking endpoints for improving QueryWorks search relevance. Walkthrough of embeddings generation, neighborhood search, and a two-step rerank flow. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS), EU data residency requirement, and POC next steps.
topics: Reranking endpoint usage in a two-step search flow
Vector store vs Redwood managed reranker
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: cool thanks everyone for joining, i'm jordan from redwood. Welcome, can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: hi i'm maya, head of search at queryworks, running infra for our internal search product.
[00:18] Tom: tom here, staff swe, i own ranking infra and the elastic integration.
[00:23] Priya: priya product, driving the roadmap for search relevance.
[00:27] Sofia: and i'm sofia from redwood se, i'll go through the technical bits and the demo.
[00:33] Jordan: awesome. quick agenda: show hosted embeddings endpoint, how you'd use it in a semantic search + rerank flow, demo console, then q+a and next steps. sound good?
[00:42] Maya: yes, that's perfect. Our main pain: precision dropping on long tail queries and slow reranking at peak. we currently use elastic + a small, hand-tuned neural re-ranker.
[00:55] Tom: and we have 200 rps at peak but spikes to 1k, so latency matters — under 120ms P95 ideally.
[01:05] Jordan: useful. quick qual: are you open to hosted API for embeddings & rerank, or do you need private?
[01:13] Maya: preference is hosted but must meet EU data residency and SOC2. if hosted can't meet that we may explore dedicated or private.
[01:22] Sofia: noted, we have EU regions and SOC2. we also support KMS-backed encryption for embeddings at rest.
[01:31] Sofia: ok i'll share my screen, start with embeddings call shape.
[01:35] [01:35] Sofia (screen): so you can call POST /v1/embeddings with text batch array, respond with vectors, we support batching to reduce per-request overhead. here's an example request, 50 docs at once.
[01:50] Tom: does batch mean we get a single request with 50 items and parallelized on the backend? any ordering guarantees?
[01:57] Sofia: yes it's a single request; we preserve ordering in the response, and our runtime does continuous batching — it can group small requests to improve GPU utilization while keeping tail latency bounded using priority buckets.
[02:09] Maya: what's the typical latency for a 50-doc batch in EU region?
[02:14] Sofia: for 50 short docs (avg 200 tokens) P95 around 120-200ms depending on model; if you want lower latency we recommend smaller batch sizes or our dedicated pools.
[02:25] Tom: aside: we use a quantized model in-house — curious if you support 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants for embeddings to save cost?
[02:33] Sofia: we serve optimized kernels and quantized model variants; our Optimize recommendations will suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[02:40] [02:40] Sofia: next, the search flow: you typically do kNN over vectors to get 100 candidates, then call our rerank endpoint to rescore top-k using the full context and model.
[02:50] Jordan: the rerank endpoint takes pairs or a batch of candidate docs plus the query and returns a relevance score or ordering; it's meant to be the second-stage, not token-generative heavy work.
[03:02] Priya: can rerank also produce explanations or reasons for a score? we want to show editors why results changed.
[03:09] Sofia: we'll return score and an optional short justification string — note that's generated text and can be turned off for cost. it's configurable.
[03:19] Tom: what about throughput on rerank? at 1k qps peak doing top-100 reranks would be expensive.
[03:25] Sofia: we recommend 2-stage: vector DB for coarse recall (k=100) then use rerank on k=10. Optimize will give batching suggestions, and you can set an on-the-fly policy to only rerank when vector score threshold is ambiguous.
[03:40] Maya: thresholding sounds promising. how do you measure cost impact?
[03:44] Jordan: our console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards — you can simulate cost for different k and batch sizes.
[03:50] Priya: demo the console please.
[03:53] [03:53] Sofia (screen): opening console, route metrics, cost per call, latency histograms, and a compare view between models. here is a sample of a production route we ran with k=50 and rerank top-10.
[04:10] Maya: I like the compare view. is there an API to pull those metrics into our observability stack?
[04:16] Sofia: yes we have webhooks and exports; also tracing hooks to correlate token latency to traces.
[04:24] Tom: security — where are embeddings stored, retention policy?
[04:28] Jordan: embeddings are stored encrypted at rest, you can set retention or disable storage. for pilot we'll likely recommend short retention and KMS controls.
[04:38] Maya: and SSO? we use Okta, need SAML/SCIM.
[04:43] Sofia: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. apologies — sometimes our docs show SAMEL but the system supports SAML, little transcriber thing.
[04:54] Tom: ha ok. do you have audit logs accessible for replays?
[04:58] Jordan: yes full audit logs, request/response hashes, and admin console for RBAC.
[05:05] Maya: budget question — how does committed capacity pricing work?
[05:09] Jordan: committed capacity is reserved GPU pools, monthly commit with discounts; you get predictable throughput and lower per-token costs. we'll include pricing tiers in the followup.
[05:19] Priya: for the POC we want to test on a 2-week pilot with 5M queries and compare relevance against our current re-ranker.
[05:27] Jordan: great, we'll propose pilot pricing and capacity to cover that.
[05:31] [05:31] Sofia (screen): demo time — i'll run a quick local notebook. first step: ingest sample docs, call embeddings endpoint in batches, store vectors to your vector DB — we have connectors to Pinecone and we can also return vectors for you to push to your existing ES plugin.
[05:49] Tom: connector to elastic? is that the plugin you mentioned earlier?
[05:53] Sofia: yes we have an ES connector that stores dense vectors and maps text fields. it uses efficient serialization and we provide best-practice mapping.
[06:03] [06:03] Sofia (screen): now run similarity search sample, returning top-100, then call rerank endpoint with query plus top-10 subset. watch response times.
[06:18] [06:18] notebook log: embeddings batch 50 -> 180ms, similarity kNN -> 35ms, rerank top10 -> 82ms.
[06:25] Maya: that's promising; combined p95 around ~300ms in demo, aligns with our target.
[06:31] Tom: in production we have noise and larger docs; any token limits or max context?
[06:36] Sofia: rerank accepts up to 4096 tokens combined, depending on model. for very large docs we suggest chunking and using caching of KV cache for prompt prefixes — sorry, i said KV cash earlier, that's a transcribe artifact.
[06:51] Maya: got it. what's your recommended model for embeddings — open models vs redwood-verified?
[06:56] Sofia: we curate models — suggest a higher-dim open model for recall (better semantic coverage), and a faster compact model for rerank if you need latency. Optimize will recommend which model pair to use based on your sample queries.
[07:10] Jordan: question from our side — do you need per-tenant encryption keys?
[07:15] Maya: yes for compliance we prefer customer-managed KMS.
[07:19] Sofia: supported, you can bring your own KMS/HSM.
[07:22] Tom: fallback behavior — if hosted capacity is constrained do we get throttled or fallback to smaller model?
[07:29] Jordan: we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or region-based routing. can also burst to dedicated capacity if you have that in your plan.
[07:39] Priya: what about A/B test of relevance? can we run canary rollouts?
[07:44] Sofia: yes the console supports canary and A/B rollouts and per-route evaluation with an eval set. it can automatically compare metrics and surface regression alerts.
[07:54] Maya: nice. any built-in rerank scoring debugging? we want to see features used by the reranker.
[08:00] Sofia: we provide score breakdowns and token-level attributions in the console for rerank calls; we don't expose raw model internals but give interpretable signals.
[08:10] Tom: let's talk scale: if we move heavy reranking to Redwood, what's the cost ballpark vs us running an optimized BERT on prem?
[08:18] Jordan: it depends on throughput and model sizes; typically managed rerank with our optimized kernels is cheaper than running mid-to-large models in-house when you account for infra and SRE costs. we'll include a TCO worksheet.
[08:30] Maya: ok. deep technical request: can the rerank endpoint accept structured features (clicks, recency) as additional context?
[08:38] Sofia: yes you can pass metadata fields per candidate as part of the rerank input; the model can consume them in a structured prompt template. we'll show an example in the POC script.
[08:51] Tom: excellent. any limits on candidate count in the rerank request?
[08:55] Sofia: practical limit we recommend top-100 before chunking; above that token budgets start to spike. but you can send IDs plus use a lightweight scoring model to pre-filter.
[09:06] [09:06] Jordan: quick pivot — data residency. Maya mentioned EU requirement, are there specific audit/regulatory controls you need?
[09:13] Maya: we need data to remain in EU for the pilot and SOC2 proof, and we'd prefer KMS in our tenancy.
[09:20] Sofia: we can pin region to EU and support customer-managed KMS; for tenancy-level KMS we'll need enterprise plan details, but it's supported.
[09:30] Priya: if we later need private deployment, how different is the API surface?
[09:36] Jordan: same API surface; private just changes control plane and network. we aim for consistent developer experience.
[09:43] Tom: logging replay — can we replay a day's traffic for offline eval?
[09:47] Jordan: yes you can export logs and replay through the POC script; we also offer a sandbox stack for benchmarking.
[09:53] Maya: ok, let's discuss pilot success metrics: precision@10 improvement > 7% and P95 latency < 150ms for rerank.
[10:03] Jordan: noted, we'll design the POC to track those.
[10:07] Priya: timeline — we want results within two weeks after ingestion, decision by mid-october.
[10:13] Jordan: doable.
[10:16] [10:16] Sofia (screen): demo wrap-up, i'll paste the notebook and the POC pipeline into chat. also linking the security packet and SOC2 cert.
[10:27] Tom: small question — how do you handle model updates/rollbacks if a model degrades?
[10:32] Sofia: we support rollbacks, canarying, and automated regression alerts tied to your eval sets so you can flag quality drops.
[10:40] Maya: good. any performance gotchas?
[10:43] Sofia: watch prompt sizes, chunking strategy, and batching windows; Optimize can recommend quantization and batch profiles to balance cost and latency.
[10:53] Jordan: ok let's move to q+a — Tom you had a question about index refresh rates?
[10:58] Tom: yes when we re-ingest docs how fast can we have embeddings queryable?
[11:03] Sofia: ingestion to queryable is typically a few seconds for small batches; depends on vector DB and indexing time. with our pipeline we optimize serialization to speed that.
[11:14] Maya: i'm concerned about PII — what redaction tools are available?
[11:19] Jordan: we have a pre-ingest redaction step in the pipeline, plus you can disable storage and only store hashed IDs.
[11:27] Priya: ok good. Last question: do you support streaming rerank? i.e., incremental scores as you stream the model?
[11:33] Sofia: not typically for rerank — that's more a generative streaming feature. rerank returns a single score payload.
[11:40] Jordan: thanks everyone. quick recap and next steps: we'll send pilot pricing and a POC plan, Sofia will prepare the benchmark script, Maya will send sample queries and traffic profile, and we'll aim to start ingestion next week.
[11:55] Maya: sounds good.
[11:58] Priya: thanks!
[12:00] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with docs and links.
[12:04] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
